Store

Storage shape

Disks for EC2 instances, and shared file systems for fleets.

1. Core Concept

  • EBS is a physical hard drive attached to one instance. EFS is a network drive shared by thousands of Linux instances. FSx provides specialized file systems for Windows and HPC.

2. Key Services & Features

  • EBS (Elastic Block Store):
    • Locked to a single AZ.
    • Types: gp3 (general purpose), io2 (high IOPS databases), st1/sc1 (cheap HDD for big data).
    • Snapshots are backed up to S3 asynchronously.
  • EFS (Elastic File System):
    • Regional service (spans multiple AZs).
    • NFS protocol for Linux only.
    • Can be mounted by thousands of EC2 instances simultaneously.
    • Scales automatically.
  • FSx:
    • FSx for Windows: Native SMB, integrates with Active Directory.
    • FSx for Lustre: Sub-millisecond latency for High-Performance Computing (HPC) and ML.

3. Architecture Rules

  • To move an EBS volume to another AZ, take a snapshot and restore it in the target AZ.
  • Never use EFS for database storage; it is network-attached and has higher latency than EBS.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • A legacy Windows application requires an SMB file share and Active Directory integration.
    • Choose: FSx for Windows File Server.
    • Why: EFS does not support Windows or SMB. FSx is built exactly for this.
  • A fleet of web servers running in multiple AZs need read/write access to a shared directory of images.
    • Choose: Amazon EFS.
    • Why: It spans AZs naturally and allows concurrent connections from Linux instances.

Q15 You have launched an EC2 instance with four (4) 500 GB EBS Provisioned IOPS volumes attached. The EC2 instance is EBS-Optimized and supports 500 Mbps throughput between EC2 and EBS. The four EBS volumes are configured as a single RAID 0 device, and each Provisioned IOPS volume is provisioned with 4,000IOPS (4,000 16KB reads or writes), for a total of 16,000 random IOPS on the instance. The EC2 instance initially delivers the expected 16,000 IOPS random read and write performance. Sometime later, in order to increase the total random I/O performance of the instance, you add an additional two 500 GB EBS Provisioned IOPS volumes to the RAID. Each volume is provisioned to 4,000 IOPs like the original four, for a total of 24,000 IOPS on the EC2 instance. Monitoring shows that the EC2 instance CPU utilization increased from 50% to 70%, but the total random IOPS measured at the instance level does not increase at all. What is the problem and a valid solution?
  • A Larger storage volumes support higher Provisioned IOPS rates; increase the provisioned volume storage of each of the 6 EBS volumes to 1TB.
  • B The EBS-Optimized throughput limits the total IOPS that can be utilized; use an EBS Optimized instance that provides larger throughput. Mo
  • C Small block sizes cause performance degradation, limiting the I/O throughput; configure the instance device driver and filesystem to use 64KB blocks to increase throughput.
  • D The standard EBS Instance root volume limits the total IOPS rate; change the instance root volume to also be a 500GB 4,000 Provisioned IOPS volume.
  • E RAID 0 only scales linearly to about 4 devices; use RAID 0 with 4 EBS Provisioned IOPS volumes, but increase each Provisioned IOPS EBS volume to 6,000 IOPS.
Answer: B
Open isolated question ↗
